question: Can one exact piecewise-affine forcing path reproduce the existing constant-forcing two-layer EBM solution while defining immutable held-out step, ramp, overshoot/reversal, and sign-reversal protocols for later out-of-distribution representation tests?
hypothesis: The registered affine-forcing reference reduces to the constant-forcing exact solution within floating-point tolerance, preserves the two-layer energy budget across every protocol sample, and exposes a confirmation forcing domain strictly wider than the discovery domain without interpreting exact-reference execution as fitted-model OOD skill.

datasets.quality_control_policy: physical parameters must be finite and positive; malformed states and non-finite forcing fail closed

datasets.time_domain: piecewise-affine segments spanning constant, step, ramp, overshoot/reversal, and sign-reversal controls
datasets.quality_control_policy: segment durations must be finite and positive; forcing endpoints and domains must be finite; confirmation domain must contain discovery domain; protocol forcing may not leave confirmation domain

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: maximum absolute surface/deep state difference between affine propagation and the existing exact constant-forcing propagator over every constant-control sample
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: all constant-control samples and both state components are required

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: maximum absolute instantaneous two-reservoir storage minus TOA imbalance residual over every sample in every declared forcing protocol
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: every protocol sample must carry finite forcing and state values

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: maximum absolute confirmation-domain forcing minus maximum absolute discovery-domain forcing
secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: both discovery and confirmation forcing domains are required

negative_controls: constant forcing is routed through the affine implementation and compared pointwise against the existing exact constant-forcing propagator
confirmation includes forcing magnitudes outside the discovery interval so later fitted methods cannot claim interpolation as out-of-distribution performance
sign reversal and overshoot/reversal protocols prevent a benchmark specialized only to monotone warming trajectories
successful exact-reference execution emits no scientific EvidenceRecord about fitted-model OOD generalization
falsifiers: affine propagation disagrees with exact constant-forcing propagation by more than the declared tolerance
any forcing protocol violates the exact global energy budget beyond the declared numerical tolerance
the confirmation forcing domain does not strictly extend the discovery domain
a protocol leaves the declared confirmation forcing domain
a future fitted method is tuned on confirmation forcing trajectories and still labeled held out
split_policy: The exact reference uses all protocol inputs deterministically. Any fitted candidate added later must fit/tune only on discovery-domain forcing and must treat the declared confirmation protocols and forcing excursions as held out.
preprocessing: No learned preprocessing. Physical parameters come from the immutable EBM fixture and forcing interventions come from the immutable protocol fixture.
stopping_rule: The structural reference experiment passes only if constant-forcing differential equivalence and energy-budget closure remain within their preregistered tolerances; the held-out forcing margin is always reported descriptively.
multiple_comparison_policy: All declared protocols and all primary metrics are reported; no protocol may be removed post hoc because a candidate performs poorly on it.
